attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter post, in his own voice. He is not quoting anyone.

semantics.note: 'Will have to raise at least another $200 billion in the next year' is an unhedged forecast. The normalised claim keeps the stated reason (the $95B raised and the cash flow won't cover costs), the minimum amount and the one-year horizon.

contract.note: The window to 2027-06-08 and reading 'another' as beyond the $95B are fair. Two things could matter later: what counts as raising (debt, compute credits) is undefined, and the support condition also needs disclosures showing need. Neither decides anything now, because the forecast is not due.

output.rationale: This forecast is due 2027-06-08, after the 2026-10-28 evaluation date, and the contract has no early-resolution rule. The evidence packet is empty and states the deadline hasn't passed. A forecast can't be scored before its deadline, and nothing raised so far would count as failure, so the outcome is unresolved.
